corrections.subject: spanish

corrections.subject: spanish
before: The draft names a place and a reason but no time or clear invitation to the reader.
A fuller version is: ¿Quieres venir al club conmigo mañana a las cuatro? Es interesante porque hacemos experimentos sencillos.
after: The draft states a plan and a reason but omits the required time.
A fuller version is: Hola, Sara: Mañana voy a ir al club a las cuatro porque hacemos experimentos sencillos.
corrections.reason: The prompt asks for a plan, time and reason; the former answer incorrectly treated an invitation as another required element.

corrections.subject: english-language-literature
before: The proposal uses limited observations of demand in wet weather as support.
A trial recognises that three days cannot establish demand across the whole year.
after: The proposal uses limited observations of demand in wet weather as support.
A trial recognises that three days cannot establish demand across the whole year.
A full rack shows use, but does not by itself establish that shelter is needed or would attract more users.
corrections.reason: Distinguish evidence about capacity from evidence about the proposed shelter’s benefit.

corrections.subject: english-language-literature
corrections.before: The argument connects a practical problem to a testable proposal while retaining a limit on its evidence.
corrections.after: The observations support investigating capacity. A trial should also test whether shelter improves access in wet weather, while retaining the limit of the three-day evidence.
corrections.reason: Keep the model judgement proportional to the observed outcome rather than assuming the proposed feature’s mechanism.

corrections.subject: english-language-literature
corrections.before: The break delays the object of the action.
corrections.after: The break delays what the window is opened to.
corrections.reason: The first line already supplies window as the verb’s direct object; the delayed phrase specifies what it is opened to.

corrections.subject: english-language-literature
corrections.before: The opening claim presents the letter as unimportant to the narrator.
corrections.after: The opening claim says the narrator no longer remembers or thinks about the letter.
corrections.reason: Forgetting does not directly establish unimportance; retain the actual self-description before analysing contradiction.

corrections.subject: visual-arts
before: Record the change and viewing condition rather than only saying “v3 looked worse”.
Explain the next trial: reduce the border’s weight while keeping the text size constant, then compare at the same distance.
after: Model entry: “Version 3: I added a dark border. From two metres, it drew attention away from the central text.”
Next decision: “I will reduce the border’s weight, keep the text size constant and compare the versions from the same two-metre viewing position.”
corrections.reason: The task requests a decision entry; provide the actual model entry rather than instructions to write one.
